evidence: SOURCE (verified by reading frozen bytes): solution/solve.sh:1 '#!/bin/bash' with LF (python byte scan: zero CR bytes in every file of the frozen task); solve.sh:3 'mkdir -p /app', :35 cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/, :36 removes only the DB file and its -wal/-shm, and :5-9 refuse a DB_PATH outside /app. It writes nothing to /tests, /logs/verifier or /solution, has no pkill, no NODE_ENV, no npm/curl/wget/pip install (grep). The node heredoc (:12-34) exits 0 immediately when no database exists (:16), so a fresh agent-image install cannot fail on /proc permissions; 'node - "$path"' puts the path in process.argv[2]. The template solve.sh is the plain mkdir+cp; the task's extra guard is a superset. The app copies to /app/server.js, the entry test.sh:68/97/111 requires and instruction.md:13 names. Self-contained: dependencies come only from NODE_PATH globals express@5.1.0/better-sqlite3@12.4.1, pinned identically in environment/Dockerfile:9-12 and tests/Dockerfile:19-25, and package.json pins the same versions. No node_modules or symlinks are shipped, so the test.sh:72-83 symlink refusal is not triggered. The seed is bundled: solution/app/src/seed_data.json sha256 22df2a00... equals environment/assets/seed_data.json, so the app does not read /assets at runtime (instruction.md:15). There are no http(s) URLs in server src or in public src/href attributes (grep). Contract: bootstrap.js:43 listens on Number(process.env.PORT||3000) at 0.0.0.0. bootstrap.js:21-25 answers GET /api/health in the main thread before the SQLite worker is ready (integration.md: 'answers before database work can block startup'). db.js:9 honours process.env.DB_PATH and otherwise defaults to <app>/app.db. db.js:10 and index.js:42 resolve seed and public via __dirname, which satisfies hireops_rules.md section 8 for the test.sh:99-102 /tmp/submission writable-copy fallback and a non-/app cwd. db.js:61-62 seeds only when users is empty, inside a transaction (:65-85), so seeding is idempotent and restarts keep data. No shipped DB: solve.sh:36 deletes it and the frozen solution/app tree has no *.db. RUNTIME (partial): raw-evidence-index scope says the golden ran in the verifier image against the frozen solution bytes as uid 65534. workspace.cjs:16 launches 'node /app/server.js' with cwd /tmp and a minimal env (PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT=3000, DB_PATH=/tmp/hireops-workspace.db). workspace.json records all 18 groups passed, including 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding', with page_errors []. server.log shows '[hireops] listening on 3000' twice (initial launch plus the restart). That confirms entry, port, DB_PATH, health, cwd independence, idempotent restart and NODE_PATH-only deps in practice. The workbook's network caveat and the Internal sheet's 'no run-time install' both hold, since solve.sh installs nothing. Adversarial probes: (a) a broken reference that bundled only /assets reads would crash under the copy fallback. Not the case: the seed is copied beside db.js. (b) A reference whose health touched the DB would hang behind a locked DB. Not the case: bootstrap answers health in the main thread. (c) A conforming alternative solve.sh that only copies, like the template, is not penalised by this row. RISK (why true): the evidence does not show that solve.sh itself was executed to populate /app in the agent image. It also does not show the real test.sh launch path (env -i + setpriv, /app/app.db under chown 65534, or the /tmp/submission fallback) in a configured verifier run. The index scope states that the full configured grading/workload run is absent, and REVIEW_POLICY requires a hash-bound full-verifier-launch record before clearance. I found no defect in this row's source; the missing measurement stays a risk and is not waived.
